title: Geneva Rising Revisited
premise: Bram Galloway's one failed negotiation — a hostage exchange in Geneva that left a colleague dead and his memory of the final hour suspiciously clean — was supposed to stay buried. When a real-estate listing for the safe house where it happened surfaces with interior photos showing evidence he thought destroyed, Bram realizes someone from the covert network that trained him is rewriting the record to frame him before an international summit. As he hunts the seller through Zurich and Geneva, he uncovers that his polished lie about that night was implanted, not remembered. In the end, Bram burns the network's leadership by turning their own negotiation tactics against them on live channels during the summit, choosing truth over loyalty — though the cost is the last person who still believed his old story.
about_author: Wren Sterling is the pen name of a former crisis-line counselor who spent a decade listening to people talk their way out of impossible corners. Sterling writes thrillers about the gap between what negotiators say and what they know.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Between negotiations, Bram idly browses property listings and finds the Geneva safe house for sale — with photos of a room he's spent seven years pretending doesn't exist, including a scorch mark only he could have made. His go-bag is already packed. Emotional beat: dread disguised as curiosity; the past knocking politely.

chapters.title: Polished Lie
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, with a flashback. Bram reviews his official account of the failed exchange — the version he's told so often it feels true — while his handler, Ilse, warns him off investigating. A junior agent tails him anyway. Emotional beat: the unease of a man whose best story has seams he can't stop touching.

chapters.title: Open House
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Posing as a buyer, Bram walks through the safe house and finds the staging deliberately arranged to recreate the night of the failure — down to the chair positions. The listing agent slips him a keycard with a summit logo. Emotional beat: vertigo; someone knows the room better than he does.

chapters.title: Ilse's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse reports Bram's movements to a superior known only as Cartographer, revealing she's been managing him like an asset, not a colleague — but she hesitates when ordered to let him walk into a trap. Emotional beat: loyalty curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: Zurich Dead Drop
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Following the keycard, Bram meets a retired network archivist who shows him training files — including footage of the Geneva night that contradicts his memory: he wasn't outside the room; he was inside it, negotiating. Emotional beat: the floor giving way beneath a man built on procedure.

chapters.title: The Implanted Hour
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, fragmented narration. Bram confronts the possibility that his 'clean' memory was installed during post-crisis debriefs. He tests fragments against the footage and finds his lie fits perfectly — too perfectly. Emotional beat: grief for a self that may never have existed.

chapters.title: Cartographer
chapters.summary: Cartographer's POV. The network's architect explains the plan: frame Bram for the Geneva death days before the summit, discrediting hostage diplomacy itself. We learn the archivist was bait. Emotional beat: chilling calm; evil as project management.

chapters.title: Counter-Offer
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Instead of running, Bram goes back to Ilse and negotiates — using every technique the network taught him — flipping her by offering her the one thing she wants: out. She gives him the summit's security channel access. Emotional beat: the student weaponizing the curriculum.

chapters.title: The Summit Room
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, intercut with Cartographer's. During the summit, Bram hijacks the network's own comms and broadcasts the Geneva footage plus Cartographer's orders, then talks Cartographer into a corner live — offering surrender terms the man can't refuse without confessing. Emotional beat: cold triumph with blood on it.

chapters.title: Empty Rooms
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, weeks later. The network is burned, Cartographer detained, but Ilse took a bullet meant for Bram in the final minutes — the last person who believed his old story. He lists the safe house himself, walks its empty rooms once, and leaves the door open. Emotional beat: quiet, unheroic peace; truth as a house you can finally leave.
